focus_area: Background jobs — retry_on/exhaustion behavior, error-class handling, status transitions on failure, broadcast-on-failure, claim-row lifecycle; analog structural matching (BLOCKER-class).
verification_notes: CRITICAL CHECK 1 (exhaustion block) — VERIFIED CORRECT. ActiveJob 6.1.7.7 exceptions.rb:56-72 registers retry_on via rescue_from and, on exhaustion, calls `yield self, error` (line 64), NOT instance_exec. rescue_from runs the OUTER proc via instance_exec on the job instance, but `yield` does not rebind the INNER user block's self. The inner exhaustion block `do |job, error|` was created lexically in the class body, so inside it `self` == the CLASS (ExtractJobCriteriaJob), while the yielded `job` param == the job INSTANCE. Therefore extract_job_criteria_job.rb:11 `job.send(:broadcast_completion, ai_job_criteria, job.arguments.second)` is correct: `broadcast_completion` is a private INSTANCE method (line 39, under `private`), a bare call would resolve against the class and raise NoMethodError, and `.send` on the yielded instance both bypasses privacy and targets the right receiver. `ai_job_criteria` is in scope (assigned line 8 from `AiJobCriteria.find_by(id: job.arguments.first)`) and is set to :failed (line 10) before the broadcast, so the fresh re-read inside broadcast_completion (line 46) sees the failed row. `job.arguments.first`==ai_job_criteria_id, `job.arguments.second`==requesting_organization_user_id (positional signature `perform(ai_job_criteria_id, requesting_organization_user_id = nil)`). Error escape analysis: `retry_on CustomErrorAiSummary`; perform rescues CustomErrorAiSummary first and re-raises (propagates to rescue_from→retry), then StandardError. CustomErrorAiSummary < StandardError (app/errors/custom_error_ai_summary.rb:3), so the specific-before-general ordering is correct; no in-band error escapes unhandled (non-StandardError escapes, same as the analog and standard Ruby). CHECK 2 (optional positional arg) — VERIFIED: old in-flight payload `[id]` → perform(id) → requesting_organization_user_id=nil → line 23 broadcast skipped; exhaustion block `job.arguments.second`==nil → broadcast_completion returns early via `OrganizationUser.find_by(id: nil)`. No crash. CHECK 3 (bulk claim-row :failed) — VERIFIED: validation-fail path (bulk_generate_ai_summaries_job.rb:62-66) sets the claim row to :failed (valid enum, bulk_ai_summary_job_application.rb:10) and logs `result.error` (set by ValidateAiSummaryGeneration#context.fail!). on_complete counts a :failed row as failed (size-done-deferred) and still fires notify_failure/notify_complete, so the completion toast is NOT skipped. QueueBulkAiSummaryJobs:46-48 only treats :processing as already-claimed, so :failed rows are re-queueable. update_columns is not inside a transaction (job-iteration does not wrap each_iteration), consistent with lines 54/56/72/92 (pipeline rule 25 OK). CHECK 4 (structural diff vs analog) — MATCHES: same retry_on(CustomErrorAiSummary, 2.min, 3)→exhaustion-write-failed+broadcast; same perform→run+broadcast-if-requesting; same `rescue CustomErrorAiSummary; raise`; same `rescue StandardError`→re-read+write-failed+broadcast; same private instance `broadcast_completion` with terminal-status guard and fresh re-read (SPEC §7 blesses the AiJobCriteria.find_by fresh-read form). The one deviation (job.send vs analog's bare call) is adjudicated item 10 AND is a correctness improvement over the analog's latent bug. Jobs are soft-deleted (job.rb:414 discarded_at), so `ai_job_criteria.job.title` (line 54) cannot NoMethodError on a deleted job; belongs_to :job is required so job is always present. No BLOCKER, no HIGH in the feature code.

findings.title: Pre-existing: BulkGenerateAiSummariesJob#each_iteration leaves the claim row :processing on the StandardError catch-all and on job-application-not-found (contradicts the file's own header comment)
findings.description: The brief asked to confirm no claim row is left stuck :processing on any path. The FEATURE's added path (validation failure, lines 62-66) correctly sets :failed. But two PRE-EXISTING paths still leave the row :processing: (1) the catch-all `rescue StandardError => e` (lines 95-98) only logs `Rails.logger.error`+`ap e` and returns — it never updates job_application_bulk_job_status, so an unexpected error anywhere in lines 60-92 (e.g. CreateBulkAiSummaryGeneration or generate_ai_summary_with_credit_flow raising a non-CustomErrorAiSummary) leaves the row :processing; (2) `return unless job_application` (line 33) returns before the claim row is even looked up (line 37), leaving any pre-created :processing row for a since-deleted JobApplication stuck. A stuck :processing row is un-reclaimable because QueueBulkAiSummaryJobs filters `status: :processing` as already-claimed (queue_bulk_ai_summary_jobs.rb:46-48). This directly contradicts the file header comment (lines 3-7): 'Failure paths (retry exhaustion, non-retryable, catch-all) update rows to :failed' — the catch-all does NOT. on_complete still counts these rows in `failed` (size - done - deferred) so the toast count is unaffected. This is genuinely PRE-EXISTING (the feature diff only touched the validation path, lines 62-66) and OUT OF FEATURE SCOPE; reported only because the brief explicitly asked to verify all :processing paths. Do-not-fix under this feature.
findings.recommendation: No change under this feature (out of scope, pre-existing). If it is ever addressed separately, set the claim row to :failed in the each_iteration `rescue StandardError` before returning, and reconcile the header comment. Note for the report: the feature's own validation-fail path is correct.

findings.title: Analog (generate_ai_job_application_summary_job.rb) exhaustion block calls broadcast_completion as a BARE call (self==class) and would raise NoMethodError — ExtractJobCriteriaJob correctly avoids this with job.send
findings.description: During the structural diff I confirmed the analog's exhaustion block (line 20) invokes `broadcast_completion(textract_result, ...)` as a BARE call. `broadcast_completion` is a private INSTANCE method (line 50, under `private`). Per ActiveJob 6.1.7.7 exceptions.rb:64 (`yield self, error`, not instance_exec), inside a retry_on exhaustion block `self` is the CLASS, so a bare call resolves as a non-existent class method and raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'broadcast_completion' for GenerateAiJobApplicationSummaryJob:Class`. This only fires on full retry exhaustion (3 CustomErrorAiSummary failures) so it is rarely hit; the status write on line 19 succeeds before it. This is PRE-EXISTING analog code (commit f485aaf3e, on the base — not this feature) and NOT a feature defect. I surface it because it directly VALIDATES the ExtractJobCriteriaJob deviation: the feature-under-review correctly writes `job.send(:broadcast_completion, ...)` (extract_job_criteria_job.rb:11), which is the CORRECT form and is more correct than the analog. This confirms there is NO BLOCKER structural mismatch — the divergence is a correctness fix, adjudicated as item 10.
findings.recommendation: No action for this feature. Optionally file a separate ticket to change the analog's line 20 to `job.send(:broadcast_completion, ...)` to match ExtractJobCriteriaJob and eliminate the latent NoMethodError on the analog's exhaustion path.

findings.title: ExtractJobCriteriaJob StandardError rescue can overwrite a genuinely-succeeded row to :failed if broadcast_completion raises after a successful extraction (analog-consistent edge case)
findings.description: In perform, if ExtractCriteria.extract succeeds (row set to :succeeded) and then the success broadcast on line 23 raises a StandardError (e.g. a transient failure inside GlobalChannel.broadcast_to), the `rescue StandardError => e` (lines 28-34) re-reads the row and sets it to :failed with the broadcast's error message, then re-broadcasts a 'failed' payload — corrupting a genuinely-succeeded extraction and toasting failure to the user. This requires the broadcast itself to raise, which is an edge case, and the behavior is IDENTICAL to the analog (generate_ai_job_application_summary_job.rb:39-45 re-reads the summary and sets it to :failed the same way). It is analog-consistent and NOT a feature-introduced deviation, so per the structural-matching decree it is correct-by-decree; reported only as an observation. The core broadcast design is otherwise sound: broadcast_completion ignores the passed object's in-memory state and re-reads by id (line 46), and all three call sites guard against a nil row before calling it, so broadcast_completion never receives nil.
findings.recommendation: No change (analog-consistent, narrow edge). If the analog is ever hardened, both jobs should scope the failure-write rescue to the pipeline call and not re-fail on a broadcast error after success.
